threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still ask for directions to the nearest Tube station, but everyone else is giving bus route numbers instead.
Last Friday, the 59 was packed with kids playing a makeshift game of poker on the floor. The bus driver just shook his head, like he'd seen it all before.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I found my favorite kebab stand open at 3 AM, with the owner knowing my order by heart. That's when it felt like home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain will you find a pub that serves currywurst with a side of techno on vinyl. Totally wild vibe after dark!

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s from here if they can name the best taco spot not on Mission Street and don’t just say La Taqueria.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a tuxedo trying to coax a confused dog off the Muni tracks at Civic Center. Only in San Francisco do prom night and transit drama collide.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think every house here is a Gaudí, but many are quaint old buildings with peeling paint that tell better stories.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a newcomer by the way they still take pictures of the Templo Expiatorio del Sagrado Corazón de Jesús from the bus—locals just roll their eyes.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still wait for the Tube to arrive instead of hopping on a bus or cycling. Everyone else is already on their way, enjoying their coffee.
Last night on the 59, a guy was singing 'Wonderwall' like a karaoke star. The driver just shook his head, but you could see everyone was trying not to laugh.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when I saw a guy juggling flaming torches outside the Kottbusser Tor U-Bahn at 2 AM, while the kebab stall was still serving. Classic Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You know you're in Kreuzberg when a street vendor offers you currywurst topped with peanut sauce. Only in Berlin does fusion happen on the pavement.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell who's local by how they know to avoid the BART after 4 PM; tourists still ask why the train's packed when it smells like burnt brakes.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy serenade commuters with a ukulele at 16th Mission Muni stop today. Classic San Francisco: chaos meets creativity, even in transit.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: They think our balconies are just for show, but locals use them for everything from drying laundry to evening chats over a glass of vermut.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell the newcomers by their shoes – they still wear them on the metro, while locals have learned to embrace comfy flip-flops.
